title: Percentages of Amounts: Increase, Decrease and Percentage of a Total
seo_title: Year 7 Percentages Worksheets: Percentage of an Amount, Increase and Decrease, Sales and VAT
standard_code: KS3: Ratio, proportion and rates of change
standard_text: Define percentage as ‘number of parts per hundred’, interpret percentages and percentage changes as a fraction or a decimal, interpret these multiplicatively, express one quantity as a percentage of another, compare two quantities using percentages, and work with percentages greater than 100%.
meta_desc: Free Year 7 percentages worksheets: find percentages of amounts with and without a calculator, use multipliers, increase and decrease by a percentage, and solve sale, VAT and pay-rise problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: With a calculator, multiply by the decimal: 17% of 340 = 0.17 × 340. Increase by 20%: × 1.2.
body_html:
How it works

Without a calculator, build from easy percentages: 10% = ÷ 10, 5% = half of 10%, 1% = ÷ 100, 50% = half, 25% = a quarter.

With a calculator, use a multiplier: 17% of 340 = 0.17 × 340. To increase by 20%, multiply by 1.2; to decrease by 20%, multiply by 0.8.

To write one amount as a percentage of another: divide, then × 100.

Example

Find 35% of 240.

10% = 24, so 30% = 72.

5% = 12.

35% = 72 + 12.

Answer: 84

Example

Decrease £80 by 15%.

15% of £80 = £12.

£80 − £12 = £68. (Or 0.85 × 80.)

Answer: £68

Example

What is 18 out of 30 as a percentage?

18/30 = 0.6.

0.6 × 100 = 60%.

Answer: 60%

Common mistakes

  • Dividing by the percentage: 20% of 80 is 16, not 80 ÷ 20 = 4.
  • Stopping at the change: a 25% discount on £80 makes the price £60, not £20.
  • Using 0.5 for 5%: 5% as a decimal is 0.05.
  • Dividing the wrong way round: 18 out of 30 is 18 ÷ 30, not 30 ÷ 18.

faq.q: How do I find 15% of a number without a calculator?
faq.a: Find 10% by dividing by 10, halve it to get 5%, then add them together.
The decimal you multiply by. 17% is 0.17. To increase by 20% multiply by 1.2, and to decrease by 20% multiply by 0.8.

faq.q: How do I write one number as a percentage of another?
faq.a: Divide the part by the whole and multiply by 100. 18 out of 30 = 18 ÷ 30 × 100 = 60%.

faq.q: How much is VAT in the UK?
faq.a: The standard rate is 20%. To add VAT, multiply the price by 1.2.
